items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: I’ve worked with Lou and we did “Rhymes and Reasons,” “Fantasy,” and stuff with Carole King.

ctx.x: Was it rather like an apprenticeship? Then you learned your craft by sitting next to somebody else?

Yeah, no, no. There’s no — at that time — there’s now schools and stuff for engineering but at that time there was no school for engineering. I just happened to get a lucky job working at a small studio in New York. And that led me into some bigger jobs and then I decided to come to California. I didn’t have a job but I just had to get out of New York, it was getting too cold. After being in Korea for a couple of years I wanted to get to the sun. So I left and I worked at Armed Forces Radio when I came out. It…

Do you feel that you had to have sort of — I’m not sure how to put this — like a different set of ears for when you had like the Lennon Sisters come in and then you had Peggy Lee, and then you had Cannonball, then you had a rock group.
